# W001 performance report — T033

- Feature: `001-core-game-foundation`
- Issue: [#33](https://github.com/fjure/idle-factory-game/issues/33)
- Measurement run: 2026-09-24 20:09:33 UTC
- Workload source: `FoundationFixtures.CreateW001()` and the W001 definition in `data-model.md`

## Method

The Edit Mode fixture validates 1,000 independent D001 machines using the `2 dev.input → 1 dev.output / 5 s` recipe: 500 active and initially unblocked, 250 active with full output, and 250 inactive. Every machine starts with input `9,216`; output capacity is `4,608`. The two separately measured intervals are `100 ms` and exactly `6.4 h` (`230,400,000,000` Core ticks).

For each interval, the test runs 100 untimed advances with fresh prepared sessions, then 500 independent timed samples. It creates each session with `TryPrepare` outside the measured `Advance` call. `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()` brackets only `ProductionSimulationSession.Advance`, so the complete method including validation, staging and publication remains in the timing boundary. After each call, `CaptureResult` and `SemanticFactorySnapshot.Capture` run outside the timed interval. Each complete snapshot is compared with the first sample and its checksum is retained.

A distinct allocation pass runs 100 untimed warmups and 500 fresh prepared sessions on one synchronous managed thread per interval. Preallocated `long[500]` arrays store allocation deltas. `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` is read immediately before and after each warmed `Advance`; the fixture asserts every delta is zero. Result capture and checksum happen after the counter is read.

The test result records fixture-construction and workload-validation time separately, per-sample preparation, `CaptureResult`, semantic snapshot/checksum timings, p50/p95, all 500 timed `Advance` samples, allocation count/range, and the deterministic checksum. Percentiles use nearest-rank ordering over the 500 raw values. The Unity test result XML is supporting evidence; the measured environment and summaries are preserved in this report.

### Excluded costs and limits

- Fixture construction is measured once and reported separately. Per-sample session preparation and post-advance capture/checksum distributions are reported separately above; none are included in the `Advance` duration or allocation delta.
- Serialization, file I/O and UI are not invoked by this plain-Core benchmark. Their costs are not measured here and are not included in the Core-only targets.
- The allocation counter observes managed allocations on the calling thread only. It excludes native allocations and work on other threads.
- These are Windows Editor regression measurements. The `≤10 ms` and `≤100 ms` thresholds are not mobile performance guarantees.
